articles.title: Why .tar.gz files can't be combined with cat
articles.summary: The author is working on a project that generates multiple .tar.gz archives and needs to combine them into one final file using cat. However, this approach fails because cat stops at the first EOF marker, which is the end-of-file marker that signals where data ends and empty tape begins. This is because cat reads sequentially, mirroring the physical tape structure, whereas tar archives are designed to be appended to and read from sequentially, with the EOF marker indicating the end of the archive.

articles.title: Why building a Rust LSP is hard
articles.summary: Building a Rust Language Server Protocol (LSP) is a complex task that requires producing useful answers from partial information. The LSP server has two opposite ends: the server that implements the Language Server Protocol and the actual state that the server wants to serve. The LSP begins with a client sending an initialize request, which requires the server to initialize itself, but the server doesn't know anything about the project until it receives the request. Once the server starts, it sends an initialized notification, and the LSP communication begins. However, the server has no prior knowledge of the project, and it takes time to index the codebase, which can result in slow response times for users.
